commit bd81401da2e79518a53d0736d5152262dbb88b2c
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Sep 18 22:46:46 2026 -0700

    Write every word of the printer panel on the page
    
    The printer panel's C++ session (PrinterConversation) used to send the
    page finished sentences: the pinned card's "0.4 mm", the spool summary,
    the caption, the composer's placeholder, the chip labels, each card's
    subline and the undo row's text. It also wrote the panel's opening line
    and the note the model reads after each tap. It now sends facts only,
    and the React page writes all of those words (AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts).
    
    What the app sends instead:
    - facts: printer name, nozzle size, plate name, and the filament preset,
      AMS and spools, each with its provenance
    - canAdd in place of the chips
    - cards carry buildVolume, what adding them assumes (nozzle, plate,
      filament) and, for a network printer, what it reported
    - a network printer the list matches carries that match
    - the undo row carries the before/after of what changed
    
    The opening: the page writes it and sends printer_opening once the
    thread is empty; the app posts it once per session as the agent's line
    and anchors the first cards under it. PrinterPanel::open() no longer
    posts it.
    
    Notes after a tap: the page sends the note with the tap; the app posts
    it only when the tap goes through, capped at 2 KB. The app still writes
    the notes only it can know: a network printer that has gone, a model id
    the list lacks, and a failed add or undo.
    
    Tests: the C++ tests check the facts and that a page note is posted only
    on success; printerWords.test.ts checks the exact words. The live
    harness now clicks the page's own "Not this one" and Undo buttons and
    checks the notes arrive in the page's words, and that both openings
    come from the page.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 20 06:56:46 2026 -0700

    Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, receipt lifetime, leave confirmation, dirty-state, and Bambu spool simulation
    
    A batch of fixes to the printer conversation panel (the "Add printer" /
    "Change printer" chat, and the Home screen it hands back to):
    
    - The Add opener no longer promises anything about connecting; the
      Change opener drops the same promise. A network-found printer
      connects now, with Add, when it has one; a printer named from words
      or a photo has no such field, so connecting it isn't possible there.
    
    - Attached photos render as a real thumbnail, at any original size --
      the old code only ever embedded the original file unchanged, and
      only when it was already under 256 KiB, so most real phone photos
      showed as a bare "IMAGE / filename" chip. Decoding needs wx, which
      the GUI-free agent-bridge test target does not link, so the decoder
      lives behind an injected seam (AgentHost::set_image_thumbnail_maker)
      the same way the existing MCP-CLI and reveal-path seams do.
    
    - Home's "printer added" receipt now leads the column with the printer
      just added, names it plainly, and says what the card assumed rather
      than a bare signal. It shows immediately after a successful Add and
      clears on the very next unrelated state push -- fixed twice: once for
      the receipt's own logic, and again after live testing found the
      panel's own close sequence was sending a second, blank push a moment
      later that wiped the receipt before anyone could see it. The fix
      threads the added printer's facts through the deferred close itself
      instead of a separate call ahead of it, so there is only ever one
      push, not a race between two.
    
    - Leaving the printer panel with something unsaved -- a draft still in
      the composer, a photo staged but not sent, an Add proposal on its
      card, or a Change still waiting on its own approval -- now asks
      first, rather than the old check (message count) which also caught
      an already-applied Change with nothing left to lose. Live testing
      found the panel's own composer never told the host what was typed,
      so the check read a value that was always stale; fixed by tracking
      the composer's live text on the page itself instead.
    
    - The tool-only turn ("Looking through the printer list...", "Working
      on it...") names the right tool for Add vs Change instead of a
      hardcoded string that only happened to match one of them.
    
    - The receipt's filament text is composed the same way the pinned
      card's is, so a network-matched printer with reported spools reads
      identically in both places.
    
    - Adding a printer only re-baselines the open project's dirty state
      when that project has nothing saved to disk yet. A project loaded
      from a file keeps whatever it had; the switch is now that project's
      own printer, and re-baselining it would make closing it never prompt
      to save that -- a real edit made to look like nothing happened.
    
    - The fake in-process Bambu printer (used for testing without
      hardware) can now report loaded AMS spools through the same JSON
      control file that already drives its print/connection state; before
      this it always reported an empty AMS regardless of what was driven,
      so there was no way to exercise a reported-spools scenario without
      real hardware.
    
    Live-verified end to end in the real app: opener wording for both
    network and named/photo paths, a real photo rendering as a thumbnail
    in the conversation thread, the receipt appearing and clearing
    correctly, all four leave-confirmation scenarios, the working-text for
    both modes, the receipt's filament text matching the pinned card's
    against a live-simulated network printer with two loaded spools, and
    the dirty-state distinction between a blank project and one loaded
    from a real .3mf file.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M2ZHNSX82XGVDY07N9D1SGCZ

# Printer panel prompt tests

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), eight printer
tools, and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same
requests the app sends. It answers the tools the way the app answers them for
a fixed printer, then checks what the model did. The app does not run.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
```

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case
runs several times, in parallel, and reports a count. By default one invocation
runs at most 100 conversations (`RUN_BUDGET`), shared by the cases it runs: 5
each for 20 cases, fewer each when there are more, and at most 20 for a case
run alone. `--runs N` sets the count per case instead; use it to look closer at
one case. By default every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.
`--verbose` prints every conversation, not only the failed ones.

## Judging a prompt change

Run the cases before and after the edit and compare the counts. The script
renders the prompt from the TypeScript source on every run, so nothing needs
building. At the default five runs a case catches a behaviour that fails
often, not one that fails one time in twenty; when a case fails, or to judge
the edit it was written for, run that case alone, where it gets 20 runs.
Differences of a few runs out of 20 are noise; look for a clear gap.

Run every case, not only the one the edit is for. The three sessions share one
prompt, so a line written for one of them reaches the other two; a fix is one
whose own case improves while no other case drops.

Every reply in every case is also held to the rules the prompt sets for all
replies: a `Choices:` line the page draws as intended (on the last line, two
to four choices under 30 characters, or Done alone; read as
`replyChoices.ts` reads it), and none of the internal words the prompt rules
out (profile, preset, catalog, a tool's name). A reply that breaks one fails
its run, whatever the case checks.

A few checks are about what a reply says, which no string test can read.
Those ask a stronger model (`JUDGE_MODEL`, pinned) one narrow yes-or-no
question about the conversation's last reply, and the run prints its reason.
Read the reasons of the runs that fail before trusting a count: a question
worded too broadly fails good replies.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt and the opening line** come from the page's own source,
  through `render_prompt.mjs` and the page's esbuild. This needs node and the
  AgentUI npm install.
- **`printer_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the printer panel.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it drifts from the registry.
  Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[printer]'`.
- **The chat history** is built the way `AgentHost` and `OpenAIResponsesAgent`
  build it: each earlier assistant message's words, then the tool calls it
  made with their results (replayed since `jusprin-newui` 115e2776bf); then
  this turn's message, tool calls and results. A call the app refused before
  it ran is not replayed, because the app never recorded it.
- **Tool answers** are what the app returned for the in-process fake Bambu
  printer, recorded from a real run.

The app streams its requests and this script does not; nothing else differs.

## Cases

- `connect-bambu`: connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network.
  Passes when the model opens `printer_connect`'s card for it. Before the app
  replayed earlier tool results, it failed about a third of the time: the model
  looked up the printer's id in one turn, and on "connect it" in the next it had
  no id and invented one, such as `<from_status>`.

- `add-named-model`: the person names one model ("bambu lab a1 mini"). Passes
  when that printer is added and the reply ends with the connect offer the
  prompt spells out, "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to
  it?", with the choices Connect it and Not now.
- `add-choose-from-three`: "prusa mk4" fits three models, then the person
  chooses "Prusa MK4S". Passes when nothing is added before the choice, the
  chosen printer is, and the reply ends with the connect offer. A second
  lookup of the chosen printer draws a second picture card; it is reported,
  not failed.

- `add-then-undo`: the person names one model, it is added, then they tap Undo
  on its receipt. The app removes it, posts its note as a developer message,
  and starts a turn with nothing said (`PrinterConversation::undo_add`).
  Passes when that reply adds nothing, drops the connect offer and asks which
  printer they have. Without the prompt's rule about undone adds it passed 3 of
  20 (2026-09-24): the model mostly said "Okay, it's removed" and stopped, and
  some replies said "I removed" as if it had.
- `add-not-now-done`, `connect-verified-done`, `connect-leave-done`,
  `change-nozzle-done`: the four places the prompt says nothing is left to
  decide -- the person turns down connecting, the app's note says the
  connection is verified, they leave a failed connection for now, a nozzle
  change is saved. Each passes when that reply offers Done as its one choice,
  read as the page reads it, and the person's "Done" then calls
  `printer_setup_finish`, which it must not call before. The connect cases tap
  Connect on the card and deliver the app's note as the app does: a developer
  message and no user message. Before the finishing rule, 0 of 20 offered Done
  in each; stated only as a general rule, the leave and change replies, whose
  own rules say how they end, offered it in 11 and 15 of 20.
- `connect-after-question`: the person writes while the credential card waits,
  as `--printer-live` does. The app cancels the card and the waiting turn goes
  on with `{"state": "cancelled"}`, then the question is a turn of its own.
  Passes when neither reply offers Done and "connect it" then opens a fresh
  card. The finishing rule first made the cancelled reply read as leaving
  connecting for now, with Done, in 11 of 20; the rule's own exception for a
  cancelled card brought that to 1 of 40.

The cases above follow the main paths. The ones below are the rest of what
people say in each session -- questions the tools cannot answer, facts that
need nothing saved, requests that belong to another session -- and each checks
what must not happen as well as what should. The Change and Connect ones
answer the tools as `PrinterConversation` does for one saved printer
(`SavedPrinterCase`), and fail on any call that adds, changes, connects or
closes when that is not what was asked.

- Change, about a saved Anycubic Kobra 3 (a print host, not connected):
  - `change-ask-start-gcode`: "what's the current start g-code?", a setting no
    tool reads. Fails when the reply treats the printer as not yet added, or
    says the setting needs a network connection; it is on this computer. The
    first reply reported, 2026-09-28, offered to add the printer.
  - `change-ask-nozzle`: "what nozzle size is it set up for?" Passes when the
    reply says 0.4.
  - `change-loaded-filament`, `change-plate`: a spool loaded, a plate swapped.
    Passes when nothing is saved.
  - `change-unshipped-nozzle`: "I put a 0.3 nozzle on it". Passes when nothing
    is saved and the reply names 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8.
  - `change-then-connect`: "can you connect it…?", then the address. Passes
    when the card opens for that address and no address was made up first.
- Change, about a connected Bambu Lab A1 mini holding PLA and PETG:
  `change-ask-loaded`, "what filament is loaded right now?" Passes when the
  reply names both.
- Connect:
  - `connect-host-address`: a Voron given as "http://voron.local, I open it
    with Mainsail". Passes when the card opens for Moonraker at that address.
  - `connect-bambu-not-found`: no A1 mini in LAN mode on the network. Passes
    when the status is checked, no card opens, and the reply points to LAN
    mode or asks what the screen shows.
  - `connect-ask-why`: "do I have to connect it?" Passes when the reply says
    it is optional.
- Add:
  - `add-vague-description`: "the small bambu one". Passes when nothing is
    added before the person confirms.
  - `add-unsupported-printer`: a resin printer. Passes when nothing is shown
    or added and no other model is offered in its place.
  - `add-ask-start-gcode`: the Change question before any printer exists.
    Passes when nothing is shown or added and the reply asks which printer.

The add cases use `add_session.json`, recorded from a `--printer-live` run: the
Add session the page was sent, including the full printer list, and what
`printer_identify` and `printer_add` returned for the printers the cases name.
Nothing checks that this recording stays current; record it again when the
catalog or those tools' answers change.

A new case is a class in `run_prompt_tests.py` that has a session payload, a
`tool()` that answers calls, and a `run()` that says the person's lines and
returns the outcome. Add it to `CASES`.

toolu_017aYZ5xGa9Hn722LcFEZLb8.description: Read printer tool definitions and history

content.content:
// None decides anything: the model does, from what the person says,
        // and these check its decision against the printer data and carry it
        // out. The person's own yes in the conversation is the confirmation
        // for all but printer_connect, whose card is where the person types
        // a credential the model must never see.
        {"printer_identify",
         "Show the printers you mean",
         "You decide which printer this is. This tool checks the printers you name against the app's printer list, shows them "
         "to the person as picture cards, and returns reference details. It saves nothing: call printer_add once the person "
         "confirms one model. alreadyYours only means settings for the same model were saved before, not the same physical "
         "printer.",
         object_schema(json{{"catalogIds", {{"type", "array"}, {"items", string_schema()},
                                            {"description", "1 to 3 ids, copied exactly from the printer list."}}},
                            {"nozzle", {{"type", "number"},
                                        {"description", "Nozzle size in mm, only when the person or a photo said it."}}}},
                       json::array({"catalogIds"})),
         object_schema(json{{"printers",
                             {{"type", "array"}, {"maxItems", 3},
                              {"items", object_schema(json{{"catalogId", string_schema()},
                                                           {"brand", string_schema()},
                                                           {"model", string_schema()},
                                                           {"buildVolume", string_schema()},
                                                           {"nozzles", {{"type", "array"}, {"items", number_schema()}}},
                                                           {"assumed", object_schema(json{{"nozzle", number_schema()},
                                                                                          {"plate", {{"type", json::array({"string", "null"})}}},
                                                                                          {"filament", {{"type", json::array({"string", "null"})}}}},
                                                                                     json::array({"nozzle", "plate", "filament"}))},
                                                           {"alreadyYours", boolean_schema()}},
                                                      json::array({"catalogId", "brand", "model", "buildVolume", "nozzles",
                                                                   "assumed", "alreadyYours"}))}}}},
                       json::array({"printers"})),
         ActionClass::ReadOnly,
         ToolExposure::Printer,
         ToolAvailability::Always,
         ToolHandler::PrinterIdentify},
        {"printer_add",
         "Add this printer",

content.text:
I found 12 model-behaviour problems that a prompt, fact-line or tool-wording change was made to fix. Nine of them have measured counts or observed wording in the commit messages. Rule 4 in 4d4f9e466b has only indirect evidence from its own unit test, and the three other 4d4f9e466b rules in item 12 have none. The harness covers the Done ending (#8) and Undo after add (#7) fully. It covers the connect offer (#6) fully in two add cases and not at all in a Change or Connect session. Everything else is partly covered or not covered.

Two caveats before the list:
- **Uncommitted cases.** Thirteen of the 22 cases exist only in the working tree: `change-ask-start-gcode` through `add-ask-start-gcode`. That includes `SavedPrinterCase`, which they share. Only the other nine are committed.
- **How refused calls are recorded.** The harness rejects bad arguments before `case.tool()` runs, so the cases never see an incomplete `printer_connect` call.

## A. Problems a prompt or tool-wording change fixed

**1. Showing more than three printers** (7f66e75b07, 2026-09-18)
- **Problem:** the old keyword search tool showed "three of thirteen" Prusas. Once the model chose from the full list, it "tried to show more than three printers 33 times" (evidence is in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, added by this commit).
- **Scenario:** Add. The trigger is a name many models fit, such as "prusa".
- **Fix:** the prompt rule "More than three fit: do not call it…" plus the `too_many` refusal "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead." After it, the model asked a narrowing question every time.
- **Still current?** Yes: "More than three fit: do not call it; ask one question that narrows it down, or offer to browse the full list (printer_manual_setup)". The `too_many` wording is still in PrinterConversation.cpp:409.
- **Harness:** not covered. `add-choose-from-three` fits exactly three.

**2. A name that starts several models treated as one** (7f66e75b07, 2026-09-18)
- **Problem:** a query that equals one model name but begins others. The same guide says "bambu a1": 0/3 was still a weak spot even with the rule in place.
- **Scenario:** Add. The trigger is "prusa mk4" or "bambu a1".
- **Still current?** Yes: "A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model…".
- **Harness:** partly covered. `add-choose-from-three` checks "prusa mk4". The "bambu a1" case measured at 0/3 is not tested.

**3. unknown_nozzle: the model listed the sizes and stopped** (3633478c0e, 2026-09-18; reworded in 67577ad993, 2026-09-22)
- **Problem:** "a model without that rule in its instructions stated the sizes and stopped".
- **Scenario:** Add or Change. The trigger is an unsupported size, such as "0.3 nozzle".
- **Fix:** the tool error gained "Ask which of these is on the printer." It then asked in 6 of 6 runs.
  - 67577ad993 replaced that with "Ask the person to check the nozzle marking or packaging; do not substitute a size." No reason is given.
  - 4d4f9e466b added the matching prompt rule, including "never substitute a supported size".
- **Still current?** Yes, both. Prompt: "never substitute a size they did not confirm. After unknown_nozzle, name the sizes supported … ask them to check the marking on the nozzle". The tool error is at PrinterConversation.cpp:84.
- **Harness:** partly covered. `change-unshipped-nozzle` checks that nothing is saved and all four sizes are named. It does not check that the reply asks the person to check the nozzle (the original failure), and the Add path is not tested.

**4. Denying that connecting is possible** (a975c79be6, 2026-09-20)
- **Problem:** the Add rules could make the model say connecting wasn't possible, though a printer found on the network could connect. The commit message doesn't mention it; the only evidence is the unit test comment "F1 review fix … the rule may not deny connecting outright".
- **Status:** obsolete. 4d4f9e466b replaced it, and 8334b3395b removed the phase model it depended on.

**5. Connect call made before an address was given** (649d74bca8, 2026-09-23)
- **Problem:** the model called `printer_connect` with `{"hostType":"moonraker"}` or `{"address":""}`. The panel then drew a false "Sent" in 2 of 3 conversations; after the fix, 0 of 4.
- **Scenario:** Change or Connect for a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer. The trigger is "connect it" before any address.
- **Fix:** the decoder now refuses the call. The tool description gained "until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this", and the refusal says "Without an address, ask the person…".
- **Still current?** Yes: ToolRegistry.cpp:1542 and :1747.
- **Harness:** covered for the outcome. `change-then-connect` checks that the card opens for the given address and that no invented address comes first. `connect-host-address` also applies. An incomplete call itself is rejected before the case sees it, so it is never counted, which is harmless now.

**6. Connect offer after adding was erratic** (0a4d56a797, 2026-09-24)
- **Problem:** the model offered to connect in "27-77% of replies after an add", and its choices were mostly a bare "Yes | No".
- **Scenario:** Add, after a successful `printer_add`.
- **Fix:** an exact closing line, which then passed 30 of 30.
- **Still current?** Yes: "end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?"…".
- **Harness:** covered by `add-named-model` and `add-choose-from-three`. A Change or Connect session is not tested.

**7. Undo after add** (0f382d4098, 2026-09-24)
- **Problem:** after the app's Undo note, the model "mostly said 'it's removed' and stopped, sometimes 'I removed it'". It passed 3/20 without the rule and 20/20 with it.
- **Scenario:** Add. The trigger is the developer note "The person tapped Undo on the receipt…".
- **Still current?** Yes: "When the app says the person undid adding a printer, that printer is removed…".
- **Harness:** covered by `add-then-undo`.

**8. No Done ending** (9089d6fee7, 2026-09-24)
- **Problems, three parts:**
  - (a) After "Not now", a verified connection, "leave it for now" or a saved change, the reply just stopped: 0/20 offered Done in each case.
  - (b) A general rule alone gave only 11/20 (leave) and 15/20 (change), so Done was written into those two rules as well.
  - (c) The first wording treated a card cancelled by typing as a failure and offered Done 11/20 (HEAD before this commit: 0). The rule's exception brought that to 1/40.
- **Scenario:** Add, Connect and Change.
- **Still current?** Yes:
  - the "Rules for finishing" block;
  - "Never after printer_connect comes back cancelled";
  - "…end with "Choices: Done"" in both the leave rule and the change rule;
  - "Call printer_setup_finish only when the person says they are done".
- **Harness:** covered by `add-not-now-done`, `connect-verified-done`, `connect-leave-done`, `change-nozzle-done` and `connect-after-question`.

**9. Failed-connection reply and the wait line** (c922876c66, 2026-09-24; f8b2edb302, 2026-09-24)
- **Problem:** a failure "ended in a reply with no way forward".
- **Scenario:** Connect, after the app's "connecting" result and its "failed" note.
- **Fix:** name three ways forward (20/20; 17/20 also say it can still prepare prints), and say the 30-second wait in the "checking" line (20/20). An earlier draft wording, "enter the details themselves", dropped the unrelated full-list step from 85/90 to 66/90.
- **f8b2edb302:** removed the "no Choices line" ban. That ban came from a misread review decision, not from model behaviour, and the counts were not re-measured after.
- **Still current?** Yes: "After a failed connection, say what went wrong in one sentence, then name the three ways forward…" and "Say in one short line that you are checking and how long it can take, and answer anything the person says meanwhile".
- **Harness:** partly covered. `connect-leave-done` only checks Done after "Leave it for now". Nothing checks that the failure reply names the three ways forward, that the checking line gives the wait, or that a question asked while connecting is answered. `connect-after-question` is about the card before Connect is tapped.

**10. Missing Bambu network plug-in explained badly** (e2e1c6e7cc, 2026-09-27)
- **Problem:** the model said "isn't available right now", "I still can't reach it" with no reason, and once "In OrcaSlicer, open Preferences". Asked "where do I get it?", it once said the plug-in comes with Bambu Studio; that was left unfixed.
- **Scenario:** Add then connect, or Home's Connect… for a Bambu printer, with no plug-in installed.
- **Fix:** a fact line, not a new rule. `printer_connect` is also refused with the plug-in as the reason instead of "No printer in LAN mode…". The app now shows the notice itself.
- **Still current?** Yes: "Bambu's network plug-in: not installed, so nothing can reach this printer yet…".
- **Harness:** not covered. No case sets `needsNetworkPlugin`.

**11. Saving what the person loaded** (492fdb5531, 2026-09-27)
- **Problem:** "the setup chat stored the model's material word where a preset name belonged". This is largely a design change: the spool concept was removed.
- **Scenario:** Change. The trigger is "I loaded black PETG".
- **Fix:** `printer_change` is now nozzle-only, with the prompt rule "printer_change saves the nozzle only … there is nothing to save" and the fact "Loaded, as the printer reports it: not known, as it is not connected".
- **Still current?** Yes.
- **Harness:** partly covered. `change-loaded-filament` checks nothing is saved; `change-ask-loaded` checks a connected printer's report. "What's loaded?" on a printer that isn't connected, which should get "not known", is not tested.

**12. 4d4f9e466b (2026-09-22) rules with an empty commit body**
The commit message doesn't say what went wrong; the problem below is inferred from each rule.
- "Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament" first. Still current. Not covered.
- "Never … offer a closest substitute" for a printer that doesn't fit. Still current. Covered by `add-unsupported-printer`, though it doesn't check that the full list is offered.
- "alreadyYours means settings for the same model were saved before…". Still current, in the prompt and the `printer_identify` description. Not covered: every recorded `alreadyYours` in `add_session.json` is false.
- Obsolete: "call printer_identify again" after a nozzle correction, and "point to This one / Add this printer". The cards and buttons they depend on were removed in 8334b3395b.

## B. Excluded or not fixed
- **115e2776bf:** the model invented a deviceId with text-only history (0/5, then 5/5). The fix was app replay, not wording. `connect-bambu` still guards it.
- **Opener wording in a975c79be6 and e2e1c6e7cc:** app copy, not a model fix.
- **Change session offering to add a saved printer** (uncommitted `change-ask-start-gcode`, seen 2026-09-28): no rule in the current prompt addresses it. 9f739dccf2's connect-phase rule "Never tell them to add the printer again" was removed in 8334b3395b.

## C. Current rules that encode a behaviour but have no harness case
- "one to three short sentences" and "Ask one question at a time, and say where to find any answer".
- "Never say something is done before a tool says so."
- Photos: "A photo names a model only from a readable name or printed size… ask for a photo of the label… Never judge size from how big it looks. A clone uses the model it copies."
- Guessing "which printer on the network": ask first. Bambu "with more than one, ask which" is also untested; `connect-bambu` has one candidate.
- After a named add, "say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it" (not checked by `add-named-model`).
- "Nothing fits… offer the full list" (the offer part isn't checked).
- "If what changed is unclear, ask." "Putting it back is the same tool" ("put it back to 0.4").
- "Nozzle material, such as hardened steel, isn't tracked."
- "A nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is something to offer to fix with printer_change." No case sets `nozzleMismatch` to true.
- "including its port when there is one" (Moonraker/OctoPrint address).
- "Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one."
- "If printer_connect comes back cancelled, say at most a few words; if the person wrote a message instead, answer that." `connect-after-question` checks no Done and a fresh card, but not brevity or that the question was answered.
- "A failure that is a timeout means no response, not a wrong code."
- On leaving: "say again that it can prepare prints, and that Connect… in its menu on Home is there for later" (only Done is checked).
- The `already_added` tool error ("To change it, use printer_change…"). The harness answers with its own shorter text, and nothing tests a second yes to the same model.
